correctness.rationale: The all-order odd case follows by exact threshold calculations and a cyclic-run identity Kprime=m+1-a-b; equality forces one doubled zero (or complementary doubled one), hence 2N+2 fixed states and tau at most two, sharp on 1^m0^(m+1). In the even case, reflection-complement symmetry preserves K=m and induces exact local minority; the two closed-form block transitions and the increasing equal-bond count give a first entrance time m-2. The packaged direct graph-edge enumerator and independent pattern checker passed their stated finite ranges. They supplement, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The same natural vertex-transitive almost-complete graph family has bounded two-step settling and a complete 2N+2 fixed census in odd order, but explicit linearly long entrance to a two-cycle in even order. The balancing reduction exposes how effectively local minority dynamics survives on diameter-two graphs of degree N-3. This is a meaningful worst-case boundary on interpretations of rapid dense-random-graph majority stabilization, not a tuned finite parameter or a simple rephrasing of eventual-period-two.
